concepts.name: HTTP statelessness
concepts.description: HTTP carries no memory between requests; every auth mechanism exists to re-establish identity on each one.

concepts.name: Cookies
concepts.description: Key-value pairs the browser stores per origin and replays automatically on matching requests.

concepts.name: Cookie attributes
concepts.description: Domain, Path, Expires/Max-Age, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite — each narrows when the browser will send the cookie.

concepts.name: Password hashing
concepts.description: Storing a slow salted hash (bcrypt/argon2) rather than the password, so a database leak is not an account leak.

concepts.name: HTTPS and TLS
concepts.description: Transport encryption; without it every credential and token is readable in transit.

concepts.name: base64url encoding
concepts.description: URL-safe encoding used by JWT segments — encoding, not encryption, and trivially reversible.

concepts.name: Authentication vs authorization
concepts.description: Who you are versus what you may do; conflating them is a common source of privilege bugs.

concepts.name: Server-side sessions
concepts.description: Server stores session state, the client holds only an opaque session id in a cookie.

concepts.name: Token-based auth
concepts.description: The client holds a self-describing credential the server validates without a session store lookup.

concepts.name: JWT structure
concepts.description: header.payload.signature — three base64url segments, the first two readable by anyone.

concepts.name: JWT signing
concepts.description: HMAC or asymmetric signature proving the token was issued by someone holding the key.

concepts.name: Bearer token scheme
concepts.description: Authorization: Bearer <token> — possession alone is authority, which is exactly the risk.

concepts.name: HttpOnly cookies
concepts.description: Marks a cookie unreadable from JavaScript, removing the easiest XSS token-theft path.

concepts.name: Secure cookie flag
concepts.description: Restricts a cookie to HTTPS connections so it never crosses the wire in cleartext.

concepts.name: SameSite cookies
concepts.description: Lax/Strict/None controls whether the browser attaches a cookie to cross-site requests — the main structural CSRF defence.

concepts.name: Access tokens
concepts.description: Short-lived credential presented on each API call; short life is what limits the blast radius of theft.

concepts.name: Refresh tokens
concepts.description: Long-lived credential exchanged for new access tokens, so the powerful credential is used rarely.

concepts.name: CORS basics
concepts.description: Browser-enforced rules for cross-origin requests, including whether credentials may be attached.

concepts.name: Auth middleware
concepts.description: The request-pipeline stage that verifies the credential and attaches the identity to the request.

concepts.name: Sessions vs tokens: tradeoffs
concepts.description: Revocability and server state versus statelessness and horizontal scale — there is no free option.

concepts.name: JWT expiry and claims
concepts.description: exp, iat, nbf, aud, iss — validating all of them, not just the signature.

concepts.name: Token storage tradeoffs
concepts.description: localStorage, memory, or httpOnly cookie — each trades an XSS exposure against a CSRF exposure.

concepts.name: CSRF
concepts.description: Forcing a browser to make an authenticated request it did not intend, exploiting automatic cookie attachment.

concepts.name: XSS token theft
concepts.description: Injected script reading any credential the JavaScript context can reach.

concepts.name: Auth middleware ordering
concepts.description: Body parsing, CORS, auth and route handlers must run in an order that never leaves a route unprotected.

concepts.name: Refresh token rotation
concepts.description: Issuing a new refresh token on every use so a stolen one becomes detectable and short-lived.

concepts.name: Role-based access control
concepts.description: Authorization decided by role assignments rather than per-user checks scattered through handlers.

concepts.name: OAuth2 authorization code flow
concepts.description: Delegated authorization via a redirect and a back-channel code exchange.

concepts.name: PKCE
concepts.description: Proof Key for Code Exchange — binds the code exchange to the client that started the flow, defeating code interception.

concepts.name: JWT revocation
concepts.description: The core weakness of stateless tokens: you cannot un-issue one without reintroducing server state.

concepts.name: Session fixation
concepts.description: Attacker pre-sets a session id and waits for the victim to authenticate into it; regenerate on login.

concepts.name: Token replay detection
concepts.description: Detecting reuse of a rotated refresh token as a theft signal, and killing the whole token family.

concepts.name: Signing key rotation and JWKS
concepts.description: Publishing and rotating signing keys with `kid` so verification survives a key change without downtime.
